original.target_description: Experiment 2: high versus low probability of obtaining a mug; multiple WTA outcomes and tests, unresolved target correspondence.

notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text identifies Expectations as Endowments: Evidence on Reference-Dependent Preferences from Exchange and Valuation Experiments, by Keith M. Marzilli Ericson and Andreas Fuster, dated November 9, 2010. Header metadata supplies DOI 10.1093/qje/qjr034 and a Dropbox working-paper PDF URL. This is a substantive primary author working paper with experiments, results, tables, and appendices through printed p. 46, not an abstract or secondary account. Title/authors match the neutral 2011 QJE reference, but publication year/version differ; the supplied metadata does not independently establish equivalence to the final published version. No PDF was supplied. Target identification: original study 2 and description Expectations and reference points identify Experiment 2, but no original locator selects its outcome transformation or test. Mean difference alone cannot distinguish raw mug WTA, mug-minus-pen WTA, log mug WTA, or log mug-minus-log pen WTA. Hence all assigned positive values remain null and target_match remains null. Candidates, not selected extractions: printed pp. 17–18 report raw mug means $4.12 and $3.74, p=0.44 (unequal-variance two-sided t-test); raw within-subject mug-minus-pen means $0.92 and $0.02, p=0.058 (same t-test type); log mug means 1.30 and 1.11, p=0.17 (t-test); log mug-minus-log pen means 0.33 and 0.01, p=0.03 (t-test). Footnote 27 separately gives Fisher-Pitman p=0.02 and Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney p=0.09 for the latter contrast; these must not be substituted for the t-test p. No difference of printed means was computed as an effect size. Table 2 (p. 32) separately prints treatment coefficients .194, .266, .306, .308, .290 across five models (not mean differences to be converted), model N 106, 104, 104, 104, 106, with significance thresholds *p < 0.1, **p < 0.05, ***p < 0.01; these coefficients cannot resolve target identity. Candidate N roles: p. 16 gives 112 participating students; p. 17 explicitly assigns 52 to high and 60 to low treatment, an exhaustive mutually exclusive allocation. Conditional candidate analytic N for the untransformed comparisons is 52 + 60 = 112 participants, with no raw-test exclusion described. Footnote 27 states five high-treatment and three low-treatment subjects have zero WTA for either item and are dropped when using ln(WTA); conditional candidate for the joint log contrast is (52 - 5) + (60 - 3) = 104. Table 2 documents model-specific analytic N 104/106 and notes two zero-pen-WTA exclusions for log-pen models. These are candidates only because no critical target test is selected. Appendix B.2 and Table A.2 (pp. 44–46) add further log/levels robustness specifications, with N 104 or 112, and cannot resolve the absent locator. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders; no replication source was read.
